structured_output.concept_subject: An English market-town chandlery seen from the street. A red-brick ground storey stands on a grey stone-brick plinth with long-and-short quoins. A five-wide glazed shop bay projects at the centre, full of lit candles, under a dark-oak fascia and a "CHANDLER" sign. Beside it are a dark-oak shop door and a family door with a stone hood and a hanging lantern. Above, on upside-down dark-oak stair brackets, a jettied upper storey projects over the pavement. It is near-black dark-oak framing around white calcite panels, with mirrored braces and paired windows with flower boxes. A 45° grey slate roof with two gabled dormers caps it. A hanging candle sign swings from the west corner on a fence arm. A tall brick chimney with a deepslate band and a smoking campfire cap rises against the east gable. Behind the house is a single-storey brick workshop with a steep slate roof and a taller signal-fire chimney at its south gable, and an open dark-oak drying lean-to of candle racks beside it. At the back is a yard of four beehives, a flower bed, a woodpile, tallow barrels and an apple tree, all behind a spruce picket fence. The street is cobblestone and gravel with a stone-brick kerb and a polished-andesite pavement.
